title: Manual handling, wet floors and site hygiene
audience: Car detailers and supervisors who set up washing and detailing sites, including mobile jobs at homes and offices.
learningOutcomes: Identify the manual handling risks in a detailing job and set up the work to reduce them.
Control slip risks on wet driveways, floors and paved areas, using footwear and clean-up.
Keep the work area clear of hoses, cords and spills, and report spills promptly.

instruction.heading: Manual handling in detailing
instruction.body: Detailing involves repeated, sustained and awkward movement. Safe Work Australia describes hazardous manual tasks as those with repetitive movement, high or sudden force, sustained or awkward postures, or vibration, and names musculoskeletal disorders such as strains, back injuries and nerve compression as the risk. In detailing, the common tasks are lifting buckets and pressure equipment, carrying kits between vehicles, bending to clean wheels and lower panels, and holding a machine over a bonnet for long periods. The duty is to assess and manage these risks, and to consult workers as far as is reasonably possible. The best control is to design the task out. Use a trolley for kits, fill buckets to a sensible level, arrange the vehicle and the work so the operator is not bent or reaching for long periods, and rotate buffing with other tasks. Where a task cannot be designed out, use mechanical aids, job rotation and training in the method.

instruction.heading: Slips on wet ground
instruction.body: Wet driveways, forecourts, garage floors and the paved ground under a car are common slip surfaces. Safe Work Australia lists polished, wet or greasy floors among the causes of slips, and notes that wet or slippery surfaces are hazards that can cause falls. A detailing site adds soap, wax and polish residue, which makes a wet surface more slippery than water alone. Control the risk at the source: keep the wash area clear, plan a clear route for hoses, sweep loose grit and water where it is safe, and dry the floor when work is finished. Clean up any spill as it happens, not at the end of the job. Set up the wash area on the most level ground available. Where a slope cannot be avoided, plan the water so it runs away from the work area and the route to the vehicle.

instruction.heading: Footwear and housekeeping
instruction.body: Use slip-resistant footwear suited to the work, and check that it is in good condition. Safe Work Australia guidance says tread should be deep enough to penetrate surface water in wet conditions, and that urethane and rubber soles are more slip resistant than vinyl and leather. Keep cords and hoses off walkways, because a hose across a path is a trip hazard. Store products and equipment on a tray or shelf, not on the floor, and set up a dry, clean place for breaks. Working in wet boots for a whole shift reduces grip, so dry the feet and change socks at a break; this is working practice. Keep absorbent material or a spill kit on site, and treat any product spill as both a chemical hazard and a slip hazard.

instruction.heading: Mobile and home-site hazards
instruction.body: On a customer's driveway, the surface, the gradient, traffic, and the presence of children or pets are site hazards. Carry out a quick site check on arrival and record the hazards in the job file, with a clear route for equipment and a safe area for the owner and others to stay away from the work. Do not let customers or children walk through wet work areas. Use a trolley or a second person for heavy items, rather than carrying a full bucket up a step or kerb. Lift from a close position with a straight back, and ask for help when a load is awkward; this is working practice.

procedure: Complete a site check on arrival, and record the surface, the gradient, the traffic and the people nearby.
Plan the route for equipment and hoses, and keep both out of walkways.
Set up the kit on a trolley or with a second person for heavy items.
Arrange the vehicle and the work so the operator is not bent or reaching for long periods, and rotate tasks.
Keep the floor clear and dry, and clean up spills as they happen.
Check footwear before the shift, and replace worn footwear.
Record any near miss, strain or fall, with the action taken.

workedExamples.situation: A mobile job on a sloped, wet driveway. The technician plans to drag the pressure equipment up the slope, with the hose across the path, and wash the lower wheels standing on the wet concrete.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you change before starting?
workedExamples.reasoning: Move the equipment on a trolley or with a second person, not by dragging it. Route the hose along the edge of the work area, out of the walkway, and secure it. Work the lower wheels from a dry standing spot where possible, and keep the wet area clear of the path. Dry the standing area when finished, and record the site hazards and the controls in the job file.

workedExamples.situation: A worker has been buffing for two hours, kneeling on a wet floor, and reports a sore lower back.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop the task and let the worker rest. Review the task design: change to a standing position with a dry mat that does not create a trip hazard, rotate buffing with dry tasks, and reduce the time bent. Record the report, and refer the worker for advice if the pain persists. Review the job plan before the next shift.

equipmentAndPpe: Slip-resistant footwear with suitable tread, in good condition.
Hose clips and cord management for the work area.
Drying towels and a dry, clean break area.

commonErrors.error: Dragging equipment instead of using a trolley or a second person.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a trolley or a second person for every heavy item.

commonErrors.error: Leaving hoses and cords across the walkway.
commonErrors.prevention: Route them along the edge of the work area and secure them.
Dry and clean as you go, and report every spill.
Check tread before each shift, and replace worn footwear.
Rotate tasks and reduce the time in awkward postures.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Employers must assess and manage the risks of hazardous manual tasks and consult workers as far as reasonably possible (Safe Work Australia, manual tasks).

Slip controls include keeping floors clear and dry, and using slip-resistant footwear with suitable tread (Safe Work Australia, slips, trips and falls). Height-work rules are not covered in this lesson, which deals with ground-level work.

qualityStandard: Each job has a recorded site check that includes slip and manual handling controls.
No hose or cord crosses a walkway, and spills are cleaned as they happen.
Footwear meets the site standard, and worn footwear is replaced.
documentationEvidence: Site check sheet with hazards and controls.
Incident or near-miss record for falls, strains and spills, with the action taken.
summary: Design the task so the operator is not bent or reaching for long periods.
Keep floors and walkways clear and dry, and clean up spills as they happen.
Use slip-resistant footwear, and report every near miss.

knowledgeChecks.question: A technician plans to drag a loaded pressure washer across a wet driveway. What is the better approach?
options: Use a trolley or a second person, and route the hose out of the walkway
Drag it quickly to save time, since the wet surface lets it slide easily
Carry it on one shoulder to keep the hose clear of the walkway
Let the customer move it, since they know the driveway layout best

knowledgeChecks.question: Which is a key control for slips on wet ground?
options: Wetting the floor more to rinse it, since water helps the soap lift off faster
Working barefoot so that your grip is better on the wet surface
Keeping floors clear and dry, with slip-resistant footwear of suitable tread
Leaving spills until the end of the job, so the floor is cleaned all at once

knowledgeChecks.question: A worker reports a sore lower back after long kneeling. What should happen?
options: Stop, rest, review the task design, and record the report
Ignore it, since the back pain will pass by itself
Give them a heavier tool to hold so the work goes more smoothly
Make them kneel for longer to build up tolerance and strength

knowledgeChecks.question: What kind of movement does the lesson say detailing involves?
options: Only heavy lifting once a day
